candidates.label: The drawbar shears with the van straining, the brake hose blasts, and the van falls away behind with its brakes screaming
The blow sinks into wet rubbery hide and slops inside it; it clenches, and the guard van's timbers groan
The bells themselves: a slow cluster of membrane bells rubbed into song on the lullaby's tritones, pulsing as they swim
Tendrils lashing an iron door or hatch in ragged flurries, heard from inside, the door rattling after each
Tendrils lashing a car's wooden door in ragged flurries, heard from inside, the door rattling after each
One voice sings the lullaby's last bar but stops a step short of home, while the swarm hushes all round and drifts away
A blow on a bell of wet skin: a bending drumhead knock with a jelly wobble, and its song knocked off the note
One voice sliding up a tritone as it comes close, then closing its mouth into a hum over your head as tendrils tighten
A blow on a Climber's taut black hide, and it hissing and squealing through its lamprey sucker
The limb unfolds up the side joint by joint, claws bite the edge, and its tendons strain as it hauls the victim over
A friend hauls them up: clothes straining, the body scraping up the boards and over the tin, the limb's claws raking off
Boots kicking and scraping at the car's side boards for a hold, hands shifting on the tin lip, the limb tugging
Yanked off the side and dragged away under the train, bumping over the sleepers into the dark
A club on a friend's back, and the engorged tick on it bursting or knocked off to split on the boards
The nest destroyed: its skin tearing open, everything in it pouring out, the brood bursting and scattering
Someone hacking at a pulsing, kneading nest in a loot car: sacs splitting, fluid, shells, the brood squirming
Its long limb whipping down like a dry branch: a hard, cracking strike, the limb ringing, bark crumbs falling
Its four stilts giving one after another, cracking and folding, until it drops into a heap of branches
Aboard in a wooden car: crate slats prised off and splitting, gnawing at the timber, chewing and grumbling
His grumbling catching into a ragged man's bellow through a split jaw, teeth gnashing, then the charge
Bare palms and soles slapped flat on the crane's iron in fast diagonal pairs, the girder ringing low under it
A hound's jaws closing through a crewman's coat into the arm: the clack, the cloth, the flesh, a scorch
A hound's last strides on the ballast, the jump, and its landing on the rear platform, claws hunting for grip
A hound's paw on an iron running board: claws ringing on the plate, the pad's dull clank, ash and embers
A hound's paw on the ballast: claws, the pad, the stones giving, a puff of ash and embers
A hound's paw on the car roof: the tin's hollow knock under the pad, claws on the paint, ash and embers
The same snarls from a throat burnt out: barely voiced, a growl whose rattle is made of ember crackle
A hound driven off: a cough of ash and sparks from the blow, a broken ki-yi, claws scrambling away
A crewman's steady boots walking a body by the ankles: back and shoulders sliding, the head bumping the seams
The pack fighting over the catch: tearing and tugging, bones going, hissing and snapping at each other
A club landing on a fat wet toad-body: skin smacked, the belly wobbling, the throat sac squeezed into a croak
Its last breath out goes on far longer than a child's could, turning to ash as it goes, the body crumbling like charcoal
Greedy wet suckling in bursts, gulps from a throat too deep for a child, quick panting through the nose between
Its call's rising 'ah?' bursting out with a second, huge throat under it, then small feet and its weight landing on you
A child's quick frightened breathing that slows and deepens until it's a long rattling draw through lungs too big for it
A gout of flame thrown out of the open door at whoever swung, its breath roaring in it, embers spraying, a sleeve scorching
The fire breathing: drawn down with a pull of air through the grate, then blooming out, the shut door rattling on its latch
Its oil lamp smashing on the ballast and the spilt oil catching, its spindly half folding shut, the body falling
The lamp's flame breathing: drawn down and flaring again in the rhythm of slow breaths, its glass singing, long fingers closing
Pinned: heels dragging slowly on the boards, clothes twisting, a weak kick now and then, its breath savouring it
It sings two porcelain notes over the toy, the falling taunt every child knows, and is gone
No whistle: the coil thrashes, plates grinding and legs clattering, then it slumps and breathes out its siphon
The blow sinks between the plates into wet flesh; the plates rattle and air spits out of the siphon
Its siphon whistling broken bits of the train whistle's chord as it runs, the legs rolling under it
A bookmark taken: a page corner folded down
The queue moves up: one ticket punched
A creature vote locked in: a stamp on the ballot
A sheet slid back into the folder
The wishlist end card: a rubber stamp comes down, and a far whistle answers
A conductor's ticket punch: the click and the paper giving
Under the title: wind over open country and a train far off, its whistle once
A low bowed line falling D, C, B flat, A, so slowly it's almost a drone
Let go too soon: the pawl slipping back
A held action ticking: a ratchet's pawl clicking over, steady
A commendation: the stamp, and the station bell
The incident report comes up: a form wound into the typewriter
A line of the report typed in: a quick run of keys
